etymology: English: from software, where a product ships quietly to see whether it breaks before anyone is told it exists.
trigger: A change that would be contested if it were announced and unremarkable if it were not.
tell: A form that quietly gains a field, a fee that appears on the next statement, a policy page edited on a Friday with no changelog.
counter: Ask for the changelog. Every quiet change has an author, a date and a diff; publish the diff on a schedule and the soft launch becomes an announcement with worse timing.

confused_with.tell: The trial balloon asks the room; the soft launch asks the silence.

senses: The move of shipping a contested change without announcing it: no speech, no press release, a line on a form and a date already in the past, and by the time anyone notices they are living under the arrangement.

It works because implementation beats argument. An announcement invites a hearing, a comment period and a vote; a deployment invites a complaint from whoever happens to meet it, and the people who would have organised against it find out one at a time.
example: *"The **soft launch** was a checkbox on page four of a renewal form; by the time the council asked who approved it, four thousand people had already agreed."*
